=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m2_5 ===
- File: scripts/worktree_gc.sh
Line or code reference: lines 53-58
Problem: The jq guard was added in the last run to fail-open when jq is unavailable, which is correct behavior. However, the guard causes early exit with `reason=jq_missing`, meaning stale registry entries persist when jq is absent on the runner.
Why it fails at runtime: When ORCH_WORKTREE_REGISTRY_ENABLED=true but jq is not installed, GC silently skips cleanup instead of ensuring stale entries are reaped. This allows orphaned worktree entries to accumulate indefinitely.
SEVERITY: MAJOR
ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
- File: scripts/worktree_registry.sh
Line or code reference: lines 93-103
Problem: The _worktree_registry_emit function was fixed in the last run to write to stderr instead of stdout. However, the function writes to fd 9 which may not be open in all calling contexts, causing potential "Bad file descriptor" errors.
Why it fails at runtime: When worktree_registry_register/deregister/gc is called without a properly opened fd 9, or when exec 9>&- fails on an error path, stderr output may fail.
SEVERITY: NIT
ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
- File: scripts/worktree_registry.sh
Line or code reference: lines 150-160 (_worktree_registry_write_json_atomic)
Problem: Uses mktemp for atomic writes inside locked sections. If the lock-release fails (exec 9>&-), the temp file may not be cleaned up.
Why it fails at runtime: Orphaned temp files accumulate on error paths; concurrent GC/register operations can race on index.lock cleanup if descriptor closure fails.
SEVERITY: MAJOR
ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
- File: scripts/worktree_registry.sh
Line or code reference: lines 303, 349
Problem: The exec 9>&- close operations do not suppress stderr, so if fd 9 was never opened due to an earlier error, "Bad file descriptor" noise is printed.
Why it fails at runtime: Error paths in register/deregister can produce spurious stderr output that contaminates clean JSON responses.
SEVERITY: NIT
ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
- File: scripts/worktree_registry.sh
Line or code reference: line 490 (gc loop)
Problem: The GC path spawns jq four times per entry instead of collapsing to a single TSV parse.
Why it fails at runtime: O(N) jq invocations on large registries scale poorly under the */5 poll cadence. For a registry with 50 entries, this spawns 200 jq processes.
SEVERITY: NIT
ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3
